highlights: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol across ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API; starting with GPT-6.2, the Responses API drops reasoning items after prefix edits, so integrations need a review.
On the open-model side, K2-Horizon ships six fully open models from 0.9B to 375B-A23B, alongside the SenseNova-Loop-9B release and NVIDIA's Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B for local voice assistants.
The Claude Code team, where ~90% of code is written and reviewed by Claude, described how it verifies changes with end-to-end runs, a verify skill and a diff-triggered checklist.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, promising better professional outputs, coding, computer use and efficiency at lower cost across ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API. The developer docs position Astra for the most demanding tasks and Sol for complex work at lower cost, and flag two behavior changes: the Responses API now drops reasoning items after prefix edits, and top-level instructions are appended after input. To keep reasoning and prompt caching intact, keep the prefix unchanged and move reusable instructions into a developer message as the first input item.

evidence.quote: The examples address behaviors we’ve seen when working with GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol.

Starting with GPT-6.2, the Responses API drops reasoning items after mid-conversation edits to the conversation history (prefix edits), certain model changes (including downgrades), or changes to the end user or organization.

Models starting with GPT-6.2 append top-level `instructions` after `input` in the Responses API. To make reusable instructions eligible for prompt caching, put them in a `developer` message as the first item in `input`.

Use [GPT-6.2 Astra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.2-astra) for the most demanding tasks or [GPT-6.2 Sol](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.2-sol) for complex work at lower cost.
When the model loses access to reasoning items, answer quality can decline and the model may use more tokens to repeat earlier work.
To preserve reasoning and keep earlier input eligible for [prompt caching](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching), [keep the prefix unchanged]

items.title: K2-Horizon releases six fully open language models
items.summary: K2-Horizon is a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for reasoning and agentic work; the authors say they lead or are competitive with open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. It introduces Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA) and softplus attention gating, with the 36B-A4B model nearly matching a 32B dense model at one-seventh the active parameters, plus Uno diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a draft model. Following the LLM360 definition, the release includes intermediate checkpoints from every stage, pre-training data, training logs and code, which makes the full pipeline reproducible.

evidence.quote: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work

Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a separate draft model.
the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code

items.title: Claude Code team explains how its agents verify their own work
items.summary: On the Claude Code team, ~90% of code is written and reviewed by Claude, so the team leans on end-to-end, property and differential tests, and codifies how to run the app in a verify skill under .claude/skills/ that Claude uses before committing. If a check still fails after three rounds, Claude stops and brings in a human, and a 39-item reliability checklist is matched against each diff so only relevant items are checked. Teams running many coding agents in parallel can borrow this verification loop directly.

evidence.quote: On the Claude Code team, the vast majority of our code (~90%) is written and reviewed by Claude
To codify how to start the simulator or run your app, create a skill called verify. Put it in a .claude/skills/ folder in your repo
If a check is still failing after three rounds, Claude stops and brings in a human.
We maintain a reliability checklist with 39 items, each with a trigger that can be read from a diff, a check, and the incidents or PRs behind it.
Claude knows to use the verify skill before committing changes.
Claude reads the diff and checks only the items whose trigger matches

items.title: Gemini Tasks goes free, handling calls, bills and errands
items.summary: Google's Gemini can now take on multi-step tasks such as booking appointments, analyzing bills and shopping, using connected email, calendar and payment methods inside hardware-isolated virtual machines. The update runs on the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model and is rolling out free in the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India, with advanced features starting in the U.S. Teams building consumer agents that act on real accounts should watch how it handles permissions and isolation.

evidence.quote: Starting now, this update is rolling out free of charge for hundreds of millions of people across the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, using our new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.
Gemini operates within secure, hardware-isolated virtual machines to protect your private data and account information.

items.title: SenseNova-Loop-9B moves from preview to full release
items.summary: SenseNova released SenseNova-Loop-9B under Apache-2.0, a model that repeatedly executes shared middle layers to turn 32 physical decoder layers into 56 layer executions and accepts text and images. The team says the release beats the Preview on all seven benchmarks shown and is competitive with Qwen3.8-27B on agentic and data-analysis evaluations; with 4-bit weights and an 8-bit KV cache, 256K-context multimodal inference needs about 15 GiB of GPU memory. It is worth a try for long-context multimodal agents on limited GPU memory.

evidence.quote: 2026-11-17: We release SenseNova-Loop-9B, with model weights and code available to the community.
By repeatedly executing shared middle layers, it extends 32 physical decoder layers into 56 layer executions. The model accepts text and images and generates text
In agentic and data analysis evaluations, the model is competitive with Qwen3.8-27B
With 4-bit weights and an 8-bit KV cache, multimodal inference at a 256K context length requires approximately 15 GiB of GPU memory.
The release outperforms the Preview on all seven benchmarks shown.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B for local assistants
items.summary: NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-4GB is a small language model post-trained from Gemma-4-E4B-it, with 8B total parameters (4B effective) at Q4_K_M precision, tuned for multi-turn tool use, instruction following and input grounding in local voice and device assistants. It pairs with a companion DFlash drafter for speculative decoding and is licensed under OpenMDW-1.1. It is a candidate base for on-device agents that need low memory and fast first tokens.

evidence.quote: NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-4GB is a small language model (SLM) further post-trained from Gemma-4-E4B-it by NVIDIA.

Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B carries forward Gemma’s strong conversational capabilities and further improves multi-turn tool use, instruction following, and input grounding for fast local voice/device assistants
Total Parameters 8B (4B effective) Architecture Gemma-4-E4B Precision Q4_K_M
For speculative decoding, use the companion DFlash drafter
License OpenMDW-1.1

items.title: Apple releases FastFrames for interactive-latency video generation
items.summary: Apple released FastFrames-S (1.3B) and FastFrames-L (14B), autoregressive two-step video diffusion models that generate 480p video at interactive latency; FastFrames-L is trained from Wan2.1-14B and the weights use the apple-amlr license. It also ships an optimized LingBot 1.3B that is 16x faster than the official model with camera-conditioned control. Developers working on real-time, interactive video generation have a new reference point.

evidence.quote: We release FastFrames-S (1.3B) and FastFrames-L (14B). Both are autoregressive, two-step video diffusion models that generate 480p video at interactive latency.
We also release an optimized version of LingBot 1.3B that is 16x faster than the official model and allows fluid camera-conditioned control.
Wan2.1-14B -> FastFrames-L

items.title: Maxwell-V1-Flash: a 35B MoE with 3B active parameters
items.summary: The Maxwell Team released Maxwell-V1.0-Flash under Apache-2.0, a Mixture-of-Experts model with 35B total and 3B active parameters per token and up to 256K context, aimed at reasoning, agentic and long-context work. It uses Maxwell Block Sparse Attention (MBSA), whose kernel the team says is 6.7x faster than dense GQA at 256K. It is worth shortlisting if you want a long-context model with a small active footprint.

evidence.quote: Maxwell-V1.0-Flash is a next-generation, high-performance Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model developed by the Maxwell Team, with 35B total parameters and 3B active parameters per token (both excluding embeddings) and support for context lengths up to 256K tokens.
Maxwell Block Sparse Attention (MBSA).
The MBSA kernel is 6.7x faster than dense GQA at 256K.

items.title: SWE-CoWork drops coding agents into a simulated company
items.summary: SWE-CoWork has 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories and 11 programming languages, each placing an agent in a simulated organization with 26 colleagues from whom it must recover requirements. The two leading models pass about 63% of fail-to-pass tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments, and 31% of requirements reported as completed fail their tests. The takeaway for agent workflow design: the bottleneck is tracking requirements from clarification through handoff.

evidence.quote: We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains. Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues
The two leading models satisfy approximately 63% of fail-to-pass (F2P) tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments.
31% of requirements reported as completed fail their tests.

items.title: SPILLWAY defends tool-using agents without a model in the loop
items.summary: SPILLWAY targets prompt injection in tool-using agents by noting that targets like an email's sender or a payment's account arrive in typed fields, while injected instructions arrive as free text, and turns that into a deterministic check with no per-task plan. A call is admitted only when every target value seen in tool output but not in the user's task came from a read-only tool's typed field or a fixed delegation rule; across three backbones, no standard templated injection redirected an action to an attacker's target. It is a practical pattern for guarding agents that send email or move money.

evidence.quote: an email's sender or a payment's account arrives in a typed field, while injected instructions arrive as free text. SPILLWAY turns this observation into a deterministic floor with no per-task plan.
The check admits a call when each target value that appears in tool output but not in the user's task was returned by a read-only tool in a typed field or is covered by a fixed delegation rule.
Across three backbones, and seven task suites on one of them, no standard templated injection redirects an action to an attacker's target under SPILLWAY

items.title: ScaleVLA uses a 552B model as a robot policy backbone
items.summary: ScaleVLA connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT and compares VLMs from 2B to 552B under one training setup. Just 10 demonstrations beat a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%), LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1% versus at most 31.3% for smaller backbones, and real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10, at 216 ms median latency per action chunk. The authors argue frontier VLMs can serve as representational foundations for efficient, generalizable robot policies.

evidence.quote: We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup.

In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones.
real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk.

items.title: Accelerate Bench tests agents on whole-program optimization
items.summary: Accelerate Bench has 32 CPU optimization tasks from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions, each with a working program, workload and correctness requirements, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. On version 1.1, 16 coding agents score between 25.5% and 67.4% Score@1; most programs are correct, and speedup size separates them. Identical source code runs between 0.29x and 2.12x depending only on build and runtime settings, so agent-driven tuning should not stop at code edits.

evidence.quote: We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions.

On benchmark version 1.1, we evaluate 16 coding agents, each pairing a model with a harness. Their Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%. Most of their programs are correct, and the size of the speedup separates them
identical source code runs between 0.29x and 2.12x depending only on build and runtime settings

items.title: Google Research open-sources PaperOrchestra for multi-agent paper writing
items.summary: PaperOrchestra, from Google Cloud AI Research under Apache-2.0, uses specialized Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement and Plotting agents to turn ideas and experiment logs into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts. It works with Gemini or OpenAI models. Its division of labor is a useful template for multi-agent long-document pipelines.

evidence.quote: Google Cloud AI Research PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing. It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts
Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation.
Apache-2.0 license
if you want to use Gemini models, you need to specify either VERTEX_AI_PROJECT and VERTEX_AI_LOCATION, or GEMINI_API_KEY # If you want to use OpenAI models, you need to specify OPENAI_API_KEY

items.title: Claude-BugHunter packages bug-hunting skills for Claude Code
items.summary: Claude-BugHunter is a Claude Code skill bundle for bug bounty and external red-team work, with hunt-* skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports covering detection patterns, payloads and chain templates, plus Burp MCP integration. It installs as a Claude Code plugin and loads skills automatically by topic. Security teams doing authorized testing can use it to round out their methodology.

evidence.quote: 58 hunt-* skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates.
Burp MCP integration
Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).

items.title: Claude Platform adds linked billing in beta
items.summary: Third-party platforms can let end customers pay for Claude API usage through their own Anthropic billing, with their own spend limits, without sharing an API key.

evidence.quote: Today we're introducing linked billing on the Claude Platform in beta. Third-party platforms, such as coding agents and workflow automation tools, can let their end customers pay for Claude API usage without sharing an API key.
End customers keep their existing Anthropic billing and set their own spend limits

items.summary: Datasette Lite now runs the full server-side Datasette app in the browser via service workers and Pyodide, loading SQLite, CSV or JSON and installing plugins from PyPI.
